The BIP-39 mnemonic system uses a predefined list of 2048 words, where each word is mapped to an 11-bit binary value for compact and consistent encoding.
A BIP-39 mnemonic phrase consists of a combination of entropy and checksum bits, with the checksum derived from the hash of the entropy for integrity validation.
A 12-word BIP-39 mnemonic phrase encodes 128 bits of entropy plus 4 bits of checksum, totaling 132 bits of data.
The number of possible 12-word BIP-39 mnemonic phrases is 2048^12, equating to approximately 5.44 × 10³⁹ combinations.
Only one-sixteenth of all possible 12-word BIP-39 phrases are valid due to checksum requirements, reducing the total valid combinations to approximately 3.4 × 10³⁸.
Brute-forcing a 12-word BIP-39 mnemonic would require testing all valid combinations, a task that would take 10.79 trillion years at a global compute power of 1 exaFLOP (10¹⁸ guesses per second).
On average, a successful brute-force attack would require testing half of the valid combinations, taking approximately 5.4 trillion years.
Each additional word in a BIP-39 mnemonic adds 11 bits of entropy, exponentially increasing the security of the phrase.
A 24-word BIP-39 mnemonic encodes 256 bits of entropy plus an 8-bit checksum, resulting in 264 bits of total data and 2.25 × 10⁷⁹ valid combinations.
The BIP-39 checksum ensures that even minor errors in a mnemonic phrase are unlikely to produce a valid combination, enhancing overall reliability.
BIP-39 mnemonics are designed to be human-readable and language-independent, making them both user-friendly and compatible across wallets and platforms.
The deterministic nature of BIP-39 ensures that the same mnemonic phrase will always generate the same wallet addresses when combined with a specific derivation path.
The entropy encoded in a BIP-39 mnemonic phrase is used to derive the wallet's master private key, which serves as the foundation for all subsequent keys in hierarchical deterministic wallets.
BIP-39 mnemonics provide a robust balance between usability and security, allowing users to safely store and back up cryptographic keys in an easily memorable form.
The cryptographic strength of a 12-word mnemonic, at 128 bits of entropy, exceeds the security requirements for most modern encryption standards, including AES-128.
The inclusion of a checksum in the BIP-39 system reduces the probability of generating an invalid phrase to less than one in a trillion, ensuring reliability in mnemonic generation.
BIP-39 mnemonics are widely adopted across the cryptocurrency ecosystem, providing a standardized method for secure seed phrase generation and recovery.
